power_for_place.why: A's output generally follows the tier ladder. B puts repeatable multipliers too early, then includes a weak Tier 5 combat piece. Numbers below concern normal copies with useful setup.

A_outliers.issue: Cycling three 4–6-Attack minions adds 12–18 permanent Attack per turn, versus the 5.5-stat median, before exploiting swaps.

B_outliers.issue: One drink with three other Grogs banks 12 future stats through aging, plus 8 immediate stats including Tribute. Far beyond T2's 2-stat benchmark.
Three supplied drinks give adjacent minions 12 permanent stats for 3 Gold; roughly six times the tier median.
Two heads give six other Ogres 24 stats per Grog. Three drinks produce 72 team stats, versus 12 per turn.
Two or three attacks yield only 12–18 combat stats versus 42, while also damaging allies. Friendly-fire support rarely compensates.
Five Age-8 Grogs deliver approximately 90 combat stats including Tribute, before Chugs or extra heads, without consuming the stockpile.

power_for_place.A_tier_jobs: Early seeds, T3 enablers and T4 pieces fit. T6 scaling needs Cho'Rush or the Mog'dorg/Gordok combination.
power_for_place.B_tier_jobs: Clear supply-to-payoff progression, but T2/T4 engines already deliver capstone-sized scaling.

distinctiveness.why: A makes stat allocation determine leadership and trigger timing. B's aging adds a fresh saving decision to familiar targeted-buff engines.
distinctiveness.A_core: Contest and manipulate the highest-Attack crown through Usurp, Bicker and succession.
distinctiveness.B_core: Store aging buff spells, then multiply drinking, Chugs and Tribute.

A_has_B_lost: Mog'dorg reverses leadership; Ko'ragh rewards combat succession; Ogre Magi turns defensive stats into a crown challenge.
B_has_A_lost: Mog'dorg and Keg-Roller make hoarding a supported strategy; Ritualist enables expandable drinking engines; Rexxar shares buffs with Misha.
